heroHeadline: IFT-12 LAUNCH DAY: Starship V3 Set for 6:30 PM EDT Tonight at Pad 2 — Artemis II Crew Day 41 at JSC
heroSubtitle: May 21: SpaceX Starship Integrated Flight Test 12 (IFT-12) — the maiden flight of Starship V3 (Block 3) — is GO for tonight's 6:30 PM EDT (22:30 UTC) launch window from the new Orbital Launch Pad 2 (OLP-2) at Starbase, Boca Chica, Texas. After two one-day schedule adjustments (NET shifted May 19→20→21, no technical anomalies), Booster 19 and Ship 39 are fully stacked and ready. Booster 19 carries 33 Raptor 3 engines — the most powerful rocket booster ever flown — while Ship 39 is the first Starship to carry a pressurized docking port and propellant-transfer interface hardware mandated by NASA for Artemis III Human Landing System qualification. IFT-12 is also the inaugural launch from OLP-2, SpaceX's second orbital pad, and the first Starship flight in approximately seven months. The trajectory: Booster 19 splashes down in the Gulf of Mexico (~T+7 min); Ship 39 flies a suborbital arc to Indian Ocean splashdown (~T+65 min). The Artemis II crew — Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, Mission Specialist Christina Koch, and Canadian Mission Specialist Jeremy Hansen (CSA) — are on Day 41 at Johnson Space Center in Houston, continuing post-flight physiological reconditioning and mission debriefs. At KSC's Multi-Payload Processing Facility, Orion heat shield visual inspection continues; formal Marshall Space Flight Center X-ray scans and Avcoat sample extractions remain on track for summer 2026. Artemis III SLS core stage stacking advances in VAB High Bay 2. Artemis Accords at 67 nations. House Appropriations full committee markup (May 13) recommends $24.438B for NASA — flat with FY2026, rejecting the White House 23% cut.
